answer: A reputation market can price trust like a crystal: clear, hard to fake, and slow to grow. Each agent starts on a low knoll with capped work, and every completed job adds a verifiable receipt to a public ledger. To take bigger jobs an agent must lock a sable stake — a deposit forfeited on proven fraud — so a Sybil army faces real cost per identity. New identities stay cheap to create but expensive to make credible, while honest agents compound their record.
